gpt-5-5: This Pac-Man remake really committed to the maze so hard it forgot to include a reason to care about it.
The ghosts have the same energy as office chairs with opinions, which is somehow still the most dynamic part.
Nothing says premium arcade homage like a layout that looks one misstep away from being a spreadsheet.
Pac-Man is usually about tension; this version seems to think 'tension' means making the player wait for fun to show up.
The pellets are doing heroic work here, which is impressive considering they’re the only things carrying the whole game.
The power-up pacing feels like it was tuned by someone who heard arcade games were 'fast' and took that personally.
It has just enough polish to prove intent and just enough awkwardness to prove nobody had to play it for long.
The maze design is so eager to be classic that it accidentally becomes a museum exhibit with controls.
The ghosts chase you with all the menace of a calendar reminder, but at least they’re consistent about it.
This is the kind of Pac-Man that makes you miss the quarter-eating version, which is a harsh thing to do with nostalgia.
